tool.name: FindScriptPaths
tool.displayname: Find Hard-Coded Paths in a Script

param.name: in_script
param.dialogReference: The .py file to check, for example a model exported with Export > Export To Python File in ModelBuilder. It is read only; the tool never changes it.

param.name: base_folder
param.displayname: Base Folder (paths inside it become relative)
param.dialogReference: Usually the project folder. Paths inside it are reported with their path relative to the script, and are rewritten in the cleaned copy. Paths outside it are only reported.

param.name: out_table
param.dialogReference: A table with one row per hard-coded path: Line, Path, Path_Exists (yes, no, or ? for an f-string), Relative and Note.

param.name: out_script
param.dialogReference: A new .py file: the paths inside the base folder become os.path.join(HERE, ...), where HERE is the folder of the script, so the script runs from any computer that has the same folder layout. Available when a Base Folder is set.

param.name: path_count
param.dialogReference: The number of hard-coded paths in the script.

tool.summary: Lists every hard-coded path in a Python script, checks that each one exists and flags arcpy.env.overwriteOutput = False. With a base folder it can write a cleaned copy where the paths inside that folder are relative to the script. Built for scripts exported from ModelBuilder, which write every input and output as a full path.
tool.usage:
• Only plain string literals are changed. Paths built with f-strings (model variables such as {Name}) are reported with the note to edit them by hand.

  • Comments and strings that are not paths (no drive letter or network share) are ignored.

  • Missing paths and overwriteOutput = False are reported as warnings; the tool still succeeds.

  • The input script is never changed; the cleaned copy must be a new file.

idCitation.resTitle: Find Hard-Coded Paths in a Script

dataIdInfo.idPurp: Find and fix the hard-coded paths in a Python script exported from ModelBuilder.
